review.note: That Portugal first declined Marshall aid and asked for it a year later is written from memory; the years of the organisation likewise. Neither has been read in the cited works.

summary: The body set up in Paris in 1948 to divide Marshall aid among its European recipients and to push them towards liberalising trade between themselves. Portugal was a founding member, and its case was an odd one: the government first declared that a neutral country with wolfram earnings and gold reserves had no need of American aid, then asked for and received a share of it once the balance of payments turned, so the seat came before the money. Through the 1950s the organisation's payments union and its tariff schedules were the main external pressure on an economy the Estado Novo had built to be self-contained. It was reconstituted as the OECD in 1961, with the United States and Canada as full members. It is in the atlas as the first body that made the regime's economic isolation cost something.
